place.zh: 图书馆 · 古籍部 · 十一月十九日夜
place.en: The library · the rare-books room · night of 19 November

setup.zh: 全馆停电，他和马小宝锁在古籍部一夜。九点灯灭，十点多应急灯也灭了。卫生间那头，马小宝喘得又急又多：「我手麻了……」
setup.en: The whole library blacked out, he and Ma Xiaobao locked in the rare-books room overnight. The lights died at nine, the emergency sign after ten. From the washroom Ma Xiaobao is panting, fast and deep: "My hands are numb…"

recap.zh: 停电的古籍部，十一步，不拿眼睛走；领着马小宝吐得比吸的长。
recap.en: The blacked-out rare-books room: eleven steps, not by the eyes; leading Ma Xiaobao to breathe out longer than in.

en: Nine o'clock: the lights go out.

story.zh:
十一月十九日，伤停的名单发进群里。他不想去场边叫人一个个问「脚咋样了」，拄着拐去了古籍部。图书馆门口那块公告栏上，礼拜一贴过一张全馆停电的通知，没两个钟头就叫二手自行车和寻猫启事压住了，他只记住了「停电」两个字和一个「21」。

古籍部里还有一个人：马小宝，期中报告拿软件生成，叫老师罚来手抄二十种药。两个人隔着两张桌子，谁也不理谁。过了很久，马小宝头也不抬：「我高二崴过一回，三个礼拜就上场了。后来同一只脚，又崴了两回。别学我。」

四点二十，沈芒在最里头的角落里睡着了。四点半，馆员探头扫了一眼，关灯，锁上外头那道铁栅门，钥匙带回了家。

他是叫冷醒的。铁栅门锁得结结实实，手机没信号。身后「哗」的一声冲水响，卫生间里出来一个一米九三的人，也愣住了。两个人隔着三步，大眼瞪小眼，瞪了足有五秒。

马小宝倒不慌，掰了半根蛋白棒给他：「熬一宿，小意思。」又随口问，「这儿夜里不关灯吧？」

「九点，」沈芒道，「全馆停电。」

马小宝嘴里那一口不嚼了，手里那半根蛋白棒，停在了半空。

九点以前，马小宝把抄了一半的本子推过来叫他考，沈芒随手一指：「甘草。」马小宝把本子往回一抽：「这个不考。」一只手按在那一页上，按得指甲盖都白了。

九点整，灯灭了，只剩安全出口的绿牌子靠电池亮着。十点二十，马小宝打着手机的手电去了卫生间；十点二十几分，绿牌子闪了两闪，也灭了。

地底下没有窗，睁眼闭眼一个样。卫生间那头静了几秒，传过来一个声音，不像马小宝，倒像一个很小很小的孩子：「……沈芒？」跟着是喘，又急又多，一口比一口快，「我手麻了……我嘴也麻了……我是不是要死了……」
story.en:
On November 19th, the injury list went up in the group chat. He didn't want to sit courtside and have people ask him one after another, "How's the foot?", so he went to the Rare Books Room on his crutches. On the noticeboard outside the library, a notice of a building-wide power cut had gone up on Monday, and within two hours it was buried under ads for secondhand bikes and lost-cat posters. All he remembered was the words "power cut" and a "21".

There was one other person in the Rare Books Room: Ma Xiaobao, who had generated his midterm report with software and been sent there by his teacher to copy out twenty herbs by hand as punishment. The two of them sat two tables apart and ignored each other. After a long while, Ma Xiaobao said without looking up, "I sprained mine once in eleventh grade. I was back on court in three weeks. Then the same foot, I sprained it twice more. Don't do what I did."

At four twenty, Shen Mang fell asleep in the farthest corner. At four thirty, the librarian poked her head in, glanced around, turned off the lights, locked the iron grille outside, and took the key home.

It was the cold that woke him. The grille was locked fast, and his phone had no signal. Behind him, a toilet flushed with a whoosh, and out of the restroom came someone a meter ninety-three tall, who froze too. The two of them stood three steps apart, staring each other down, for a good five seconds.

Ma Xiaobao didn't panic. He broke off half a protein bar for him: "One all-nighter. Small stuff." Then he asked offhandedly, "They don't turn the lights off in here at night, right?"

"At nine," said Shen Mang, "the whole library loses power."

Ma Xiaobao stopped chewing, and the half a protein bar in his hand stopped in midair.

Before nine, Ma Xiaobao pushed his half-copied notebook over for Shen Mang to quiz him. Shen Mang pointed at random: "Liquorice root." Ma Xiaobao snatched the notebook back: "Not that one." He pressed one hand down on the page, pressed so hard his fingernails went white.

At nine sharp, the lights went out, leaving only the green emergency exit signs glowing on battery. At ten twenty, Ma Xiaobao went to the restroom by the light of his phone; a little after ten twenty, the green signs flickered twice and went out too.

Underground there were no windows; eyes open or eyes shut, it was all the same. From the restroom came a few seconds of silence, then a voice that didn't sound like Ma Xiaobao at all — more like a very, very small child: "...Shen Mang?" Then breathing, fast and heavy, each breath quicker than the last. "My hands are numb... my mouth's numb too... am I going to die..."

label.en: Stand up and go to him

exits.means: stands up and walks to him in the dark

refuse.en: Eleven steps still to go in the dark.

story.zh:
沈芒站了起来。拐滑到桌子底下去了，摸了两把，没摸着。从这里到卫生间，要绕过两排书架、一张桌子。

这几天，六一七的水泥地上，他闭着眼单脚站，老蔡在上铺数：三秒，六秒，十一秒——今天早上，十五秒。

他扶着桌沿，迈出第一步。右脚落地，脚踝往外歪了一歪——腿自己往回一收，稳住了。第四步，手摸到书架冰凉的铁边。第九步，碰到桌角。第十一步，摸到了卫生间的门把手。

这十一步，他不是拿眼睛走的，是拿脚上那些线走的。他在黑地里咧开嘴，无声地喊了一句：

成了！

门里头，那个一米九三的人缩在马桶和墙中间，抱着膝盖，浑身发抖。沈芒摸着墙蹲下去，没碰他：「小宝哥。跟着我喘。吐得比吸的长。」他自己先吸四拍，再吐六拍，吐得黑地里听得见。马小宝跟不上，吐到一半又急急地吸；他也不催，一口一口地领。到第三十几口，马小宝哑着嗓子道：「……手不麻了。我还当是气不够，越吸越使劲。」

「是吸多了。二氧化碳吹没了，手才麻。」沈芒道，「吐慢点，攒回来。」

后来马小宝在黑地里说，小时候捉迷藏，钻进爷爷仓库里一只装甘草的大木柜，柜门从外头扣上了，赶上过年，他在里头待了一宿。「我爸说，没事。」

沈芒想起那一页「甘草」，和按白了的指甲盖。

过了很久，马小宝道：「今天的事——」

「今天什么事？」沈芒道，「黑成这样，我什么也没看见。」

六点灯亮。门框边矮书架的最底层，斜塞着一本薄薄的抄本，《养性延命录》。讲吐气那一页旁边，铅笔批着一行小字，又小又急：「试之。吐长于纳，心果缓。」那字，跟九月里借阅卡上洇了水的那个名字一个样。翻到一多半，批注没了，后头干干净净，像写字的人有一天合上书走了，再没回来。他把书塞回去，塞得跟原先一样斜。
story.en:
Shen Mang stood up. His crutch had slid under the table; he groped for it twice and didn't find it. Between him and the restroom were two rows of bookshelves and a table to get around.

These past few days, on the concrete floor of Room 617, he had stood on one foot with his eyes shut while Old Cai counted from the top bunk: three seconds, six seconds, eleven seconds — this morning, fifteen.

Holding the edge of the table, he took the first step. His right foot came down and the ankle tipped outward — the leg pulled itself back on its own, and held. On the fourth step, his hand found the cold iron edge of a bookshelf. On the ninth step, he bumped the corner of the table. On the eleventh step, he found the restroom door handle.

He hadn't walked those eleven steps with his eyes. He'd walked them with the lines in his foot. In the dark he broke into a grin and shouted, without a sound:

Done it!

Inside, the man who stood a meter ninety-three was curled up between the toilet and the wall, hugging his knees, shaking all over. Shen Mang felt his way down the wall into a crouch and didn't touch him: "Brother Xiaobao. Breathe with me. Out longer than in." He went first, in for four counts, out for six, breathing out loud enough to be heard in the dark. Ma Xiaobao couldn't keep up; halfway through breathing out, he'd gulp air in again. Shen Mang didn't hurry him; he just led him, one breath at a time. Somewhere past the thirtieth breath, Ma Xiaobao said hoarsely, "...My hands aren't numb anymore. I thought I wasn't getting enough air, so I kept breathing in harder."

"You were breathing in too much. You blew off your carbon dioxide, that's why your hands went numb," said Shen Mang. "Breathe out slower and build it back up."

Later, in the dark, Ma Xiaobao told him that when he was little, playing hide-and-seek, he'd climbed into a big wooden cabinet of liquorice root in his grandpa's storehouse, and the door had been latched from outside. It was New Year, and he spent the whole night in there. "My dad said, no big deal."

Shen Mang thought of that page that said "liquorice root," and the fingernails pressed white.

After a long while, Ma Xiaobao said, "About today—"

"What about today?" said Shen Mang. "It was so dark I didn't see a thing."

At six the lights came on. On the bottom shelf of the low bookcase by the door frame, a thin hand-copied volume had been stuffed in at a slant: Records of Nourishing Nature and Prolonging Life. Beside the page on breathing out, someone had written a line in pencil, small and hurried: "Tried it. Breathing out longer than in, the heart did slow." The handwriting was the same as the water-blurred name on the library card back in September. Past the middle of the book the notes stopped, and the pages after were clean, as if one day the writer had closed the book, walked away, and never come back. He put it back, at exactly the same slant.
